look_here_first: TEXAS WILD-RICE — ENDANGERED: from a permitted riverbank viewpoint, look for long ribbonlike submerged leaves streaming with the current in the upper San Marcos River. When flowering panicles emerge, LOWER spreading branches carry drooping, awnless male spikelets; UPPER ascending branches carry narrow female spikelets with one ~10–20 mm lemma awn. Ordinary glumes are absent/obscure. Giant cutgrass instead arranges sexes along the SAME branch. Never touch, collect, trample, transplant or enter protected stands. Without visible flowering anatomy, keep the identification provisional.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — reference-measured field key, no-contact endangered-species protocol
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Submerged aquatic perennial, with rooted stolons and ribbonlike underwater leaves; USFWS describes clonal growth. GrassBase's morphology paragraph labels the plant annual even though its Kew overview and USFWS call it perennial; preserve that source conflict rather than changing canonical biology.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: Published GrassBase: eciliate MEMBRANOUS ligule 5–15 mm; blades 10–40 mm wide. These dimensions are source measurements, not demonstrated in the three stored photos. Do not manipulate endangered plants to expose a collar.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.flowering_architecture: Open panicle about 20–30 cm long; lower spreading branches with staminate (male) spikelets and upper ascending branches with pistillate (female) spikelets. Confirm branch origin in an intact image before placing sex-specific arrows.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.male_spikelet: Male spikelets linear 7–9 mm, awnless; male lemma five-veined. Yellow dangling anthers are male flower parts, not glumes or female awns.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.female_spikelet: Female spikelets narrow, about 10 mm and one-flowered; female lemma about 10 mm, three-veined, bearing one 10–20 mm awn (GrassBase). The 1986 species study reports 10–25 mm female awns; preserve range difference.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.glumes: Ordinary paired glumes ABSENT or obscure in both sexes; do not arrow nonexistent glumes or mistake lemma/palea for glumes.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.awn: The female lemma bears a single terminal awn, whereas male spikelets lack awns. Distinguish this structure from exposed anthers.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Zizaniopsis miliacea (giant cutgrass): large emergent marsh grass, male and female spikelets on different positions along the SAME panicle branch, versus Zizania's lower male and upper female BRANCHES. Leersia oryzoides (rice cutgrass): rough-bladed wetland grass with flattened one-flowered spikelets, but not the same sex-separated flowering arrangement. Habitat or ribbonlike leaves alone cannot certify Z. texana.
